doc.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023

title: Mixing and mastering 'Healing Time'
summary: Describes the mixing and mastering process, including eight mixes of 'Lie Your Way to the Truth'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: How many people are usually in on the mixing?

Yeah. The basic tracks usually involve all of the band, everybody’s there. We may not all play at the same time, it depends on the studio and how it’s set up. And then we might go back in and add percussion, add another keyboard part, background, vocals, and then we have a mixing, an opportunity to actually sit and mix. And that usually involves me and the producer and maybe a couple of band members who want to be a part of that. It’s very time consuming, the mixing part. And then we send it off to be mastered, and that’s a whole ‘nother process where, you know, that thing what you say where a song leaps off © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

the, it leaps out at you — a lot of that is in a really good mix, but also really the mastering too is what makes that happen. And we went through a couple of different versions of mixes with this album too. And it took a while because of the mixes. We wanted to — we had a mix sent back to us — for me it may have been too much bass on this particular song, can you pull that back, send it back to mixing, get it back, okay the guitar part is a little — it’s kind of overpowering the vocals on this track, can we bring that part down. Another track we — I think we have eight different mixes of because we just couldn’t find the right tempo. We kept slowing it down and speeding it up, and I think that was “Lie Your Way to the Truth.” That one started out really, really slow and then we realized, put it in context with the rest of the album, it needed to be a little quicker. So that’s — we’ve got about, we have really special names that we made up for the versions too. This is the quick time version, you know, this is the slow poke version.
I can just imagine you know, after listening to a mix like 60 times you’re going I just don’t know what to say anymore.

Yeah. That was usually me. My ears just get tired and I have to just throw it to my manager, or give it back to the producer. You guys, you’re going to have to decide, I can’t. I don’t hear a difference anymore. Yeah. It happens.
